title: Course Outline
summary: Hands-on training to deliver the signature Zura Massage — technique, flow, pressure, client comfort, and supervised practice.

sections.title: About This Course
paragraphs: The Practical: Zura Massage Course trains therapists to deliver Zura Spa’s signature massage through guided practice, demonstration, and supervised sessions.

Zura Massage is a holistic experience that combines firm pressure with techniques from Swedish massage, deep tissue massage, and Zura-developed methods. It is designed to promote deep relaxation, reduce stress, relieve muscle tension, and leave the client calm and refreshed.
This course focuses on doing — correct body mechanics, technique application, session flow, pressure control, and the full client experience from start to finish.

sections.title: Course Objective
paragraphs: By completing this course, therapists should be able to:
list: Understand what makes Zura Massage different and why the standard matters.
Apply core massage techniques safely, smoothly, and with correct pressure.
Follow the full Zura Massage session flow from preparation through close.
Read client response and adjust technique without breaking professionalism.
Deliver a calm, hygienic, and consistent Zura Massage under supervision.
Demonstrate readiness for independent Zura Massage sessions.

sections.title: Module 1 — Understanding Zura Massage
list: History and purpose of Zura Massage.
What makes Zura Massage the signature Zura Spa experience.
Combining relaxation with firm, effective pressure.
Balancing Swedish, deep tissue, and Zura techniques.
Client comfort, dignity, and professional boundaries during practice.
The therapist’s role: calm, attentive, disciplined, and present.
sections.closing: Learning Outcome: The therapist should understand the identity and purpose of Zura Massage before practising technique.

sections.title: Module 2 — Body Mechanics & Therapist Positioning
list: Correct stance and posture during massage.
Using body weight instead of forcing with the arms.
Hand, forearm, and elbow application where appropriate.
Table height, reach, and movement around the client.
Protecting the therapist’s back, wrists, and shoulders.
Smooth transitions without breaking client relaxation.
sections.closing: Learning Outcome: The therapist should work with safe body mechanics that support long, consistent sessions.

sections.title: Module 3 — Core Techniques in Practice
list: Effleurage: long, gliding strokes.
Petrissage: kneading and lifting.
Friction: focused work on tight areas.
Compression and stretch techniques.
Deep pressure with control and care.
Relaxation strokes and closing strokes.
Transitioning smoothly between techniques.
Reading client response and adjusting immediately.
sections.closing: Learning Outcome: The therapist should apply core techniques safely, smoothly, and with appropriate pressure.

sections.title: Module 4 — Zura Massage Session Flow
list: Pre-massage readiness: room, linens, products, and therapist presentation.
Massage start: privacy, positioning, cleaning, and first contact.
Standard Zura Massage sequence and body coverage.
Mid-session comfort check, turn, and freshen-up.
Massage end: close, cover, privacy, and feedback.
Post-massage reset: linen, products, equipment, and hygiene.
sections.closing: Learning Outcome: The therapist should deliver a complete Zura Massage session in the correct order and standard.

sections.title: Module 5 — Pressure, Rhythm & Client Comfort
list: Finding and holding the right pressure for each client.
Maintaining rhythm without rushing.
Avoiding painful, careless, or uneven pressure.
Working around sensitive areas with care.
Communicating briefly when pressure must be confirmed.
Keeping the experience calm even when adjustments are needed.
sections.closing: Learning Outcome: The therapist should control pressure and rhythm while protecting client comfort throughout the session.

sections.title: Module 6 — Four-Hand & Partnered Practice
list: When four-hand Zura Massage is used.
Matching pressure, pace, and timing with a partner.
Silent coordination and clear lead/follow roles.
Avoiding collision, uneven work, or broken flow.
Practising synchronized start, turn, and close.
sections.closing: Learning Outcome: The therapist should coordinate with a partner to deliver a smooth four-hand Zura Massage.

sections.title: Module 7 — Supervised Practice & Assessment
list: Demonstration by trainer.
Guided practice on training partners.
Supervised full-session practice.
Feedback, correction, and repeat practice.
Assessment against the Zura Massage standard.
Clearance for independent client sessions.
sections.closing: Learning Outcome: The therapist should demonstrate practical competence and readiness to deliver Zura Massage to clients.
